item.text: {"question_id":"8B.4","answer":"Xi demonstrably controlled personnel structures and linked appointments to continuity, political control, and selected professional capacity, but the supplied evidence does not establish consistently capable implementers or Xi's personal role in each appointment. In March 2023, the system retained Yi Gang and Liu Kun beyond retirement age, with Reuters reporting that analysts viewed this as signaling credibility, stability, and professionalism; it also appointed Li Qiang, a Xi confidant, as premier and Li Shangfu as defense minister (BATCH-0006-E012). Xi-era military governance formally reinforced the chairman-responsibility system, military study, personnel modernization, and training structures, although the official account does not independently verify compliance or results (BATCH-0019-E011). Anti-corruption guidance required professional training, stronger internal controls, and removal of misconduct within supervisory bodies, while research found that provincial chiefs often appointed outsiders after corrupt local leaders were removed to increase hierarchical control and oversight; neither source demonstrates that these personnel choices improved delivery (BATCH-0004-E010; BATCH-0004-E003; BATCH-0008-E008). The contrary evidence is material: studies identify a dominant Xi faction and unusually high promotion of clients, while other research finds varied patronage rather than a simple loyalty model (BATCH-0009-E004; BATCH-0006-E010). Reporting also raises the possibility that loyalty-based appointments reduced policy expertise, and evidence on nuclear modernization suggests that policy experts may have been excluded from internal deliberations, with possible consequences for discipline and judgment (BATCH-0005-E009; BATCH-0025-E031). Education and vocational programs show large-scale personnel and institutional expansion, but they are official activity measures without independent quality, employment, or delivery outcomes and do not prove Xi personally selected capable implementers (BATCH-0025-E024; BATCH-0025-E025). The best-supported conclusion is therefore mixed: strong evidence of appointment control, retention for continuity, and empowerment of loyal or controllable operators, but only limited and sector-specific evidence of demonstrated capability, performance-based replacement, or systematic correction of personnel
